ORDER 
IA (LIQ) NO. 62 OF 2024 
1. The present Interlocutory Application has been filed under Section 33 of the 
Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (“the Code”),  by the Resolution 
Professional Mr. Vikas Khiyani (“Applicant/Resolution Professional”), of Shri 
Vaijanath Industries  Private Limited (“Corporate Debtor”) , seeking the 
following prayers: 
a. This Hon'ble Tribunal be pleased to allow liquidation that of 
the Corporate Debtor; 
b. This Hon'ble Tribunal be pleased to appoint the Applicant as 
the liquidator. 
c. Any other order/s as the Hon'ble Bench shall deem fit and 
proper, in the facts and circumstances of the case. 
 
Brief Facts of the Application 
2. The Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (“CIRP”) of Shri Vaijanath 
Industries Private Limited was initiated by this Tribunal vide order dated 
06.06.2023 in CP (IB) 212/MB-V/2021 under Section 9 of the Code , filed by 
M/s. Kamal Metal Corporation (“Operational Creditor”). Pursuant to the said 
order, Mr. Vikas Khiyani was appointed as the Interim Resolution Professional 
(“IRP”) of the Corporate Debtor. 
3. Pursuant thereto, the IRP made  a Public Announcement in Form A  in Business 
Standard (English edition) and Kesari Newspaper (Marathi edition) , on 
08.06.2023, inviting claims from the creditors of the Corporate Debtor on or 
before 20.06.2023. 
4. The Applicant received two claims after the s tipulated last date for submission 
as per the public announcement. Upon verification, the said claims were admitted

IA (LIQ) NO. 62 OF 2024

1.  The  present  Interlocutory  Application  has  been  filed under  Section  33  of  the
    Insolvency  and  Bankruptcy  Code,  2016               (“the  Code”),      by   the  Resolution
    Professional Mr. Vikas Khiyani (“Applicant/Resolution Professional”), of Shri
    Vaijanath   Industries      Private   Limited      (“Corporate   Debtor”),          seeking    the
    following prayers:

               a. This Hon'ble Tribunal be pleased to allow liquidation that of
               the Corporate Debtor;
               b. This Hon'ble Tribunal be pleased to appoint the Applicant as
               the liquidator.
               c. Any  other order/s  as  the  Hon'ble  Bench  shall deem  fit  and
               proper, in the facts and circumstances of the case.


Brief Facts of the Application

2.  The  Corporate  Insolvency  Resolution  Process               (“CIRP”)      of  Shri  Vaijanath
    Industries    Private  Limited  was  initiated  by  this  Tribunal  vide  order  dated
    06.06.2023 in CP (IB) 212/MB-V/2021 under Section 9 of the Code,                         filed by
    M/s. Kamal Metal Corporation (“Operational Creditor”). Pursuant to the said
    order, Mr. Vikas Khiyani was appointed as the Interim Resolution Professional
    (“IRP”) of the Corporate Debtor.

3.  Pursuant thereto, the IRP made a Public Announcement in Form A in Business
    Standard   (English   edition)   and   Kesari   Newspaper   (Marathi   edition),   on
    08.06.2023,  inviting claims  from  the  creditors  of  the  Corporate  Debtor  on or
    before 20.06.2023.

4.  The Applicant received two claims after the stipulated last date for submission
    as per the public announcement. Upon verification, the said claims were admitted

5. The Applicant convened the 1st meeting of the CoC on 28.08.2023, wherein the
CIRP costs and IRP fees, including expenses incurred towards public
advertisement and constitution of the CoC, were discussed and put to vote. The
Applicant also informed the CoC that, during his visit to the registered office to
take custody of the Corporate Debtor's assets, the suspended directors stated that
the assets had already been auctioned by Union Bank of India. The issuance of
Form G was also discussed and put to vote. Further, a resolution under Agenda
Item B-1 was proposed pursuant to which IRP was accordingly appointed as the
Resolution Professional ("RP")
6. The Applicant convened the 2"d meeting of CoC on 17.11.2023, wherein he
apprised the members of the recovery efforts undertaken from the debtors and
identified   certain   transactions  potentially   falling  under  preferential  and
fraudulent transactions, for which the name of M/s. AHSK & Co. was proposed
as Transaction Auditors. The Applicant further informed the CoC that the 180-
day CIRP period would expire on 03.12.2023 and that revival of the Corporate
Debtor was not feasible as its assets had already been auctioned. The CIRP costs
andIRPfees incurred for the CIRPwere alsodiscussed.
7. The agendas of the 2nd CoC meeting were put to vote on 19.11.2023 and
24.11.2023, wherein the CoC, by a majority of 91.75%, approved the
appointment of M/s. AHSK & Co., Chartered Accountants, as Transaction
Auditor at a professional fee of Rs.50,000 plus applicable taxes and out-of-pocket

17. Further, the CoC has proposed the Resolution Professional as the Liquidator of 
the Corporate Debtor. Taking into account the amendment to Section 34 of the 
Code vide the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (Amendment) Act, 2026, with 
effect from  26.05.2026, which stipulates that the Resolution Professional 
appointed for the CIRP under Chapter II shall not be appointed or replaced as the 
Liquidator for the liquidation process of such Corporate Debtor, the matter is 
referred to the Board for making a recommendation of an Insolvency Professional 
to be appointed as the Liquidator. Therefore, the amended provisions of the Code 
and the amended IBBI (Liquidation Process) Regulations, 2016, with effect from 
01.06.2026, shall apply to the liquidation proce ss of the Corporate Debtor. 
Accordingly, the prayer clause (B), seeking the appointment of Mr. Vikas 
Khiyani, the Resolution Professional, as the Liquidator of the Corporate Debtor, 
is rejected. 
 
18. In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, particularly considering that the 
CIRP commenced on 06.06.2023 and the prescribed CIRP period expired on 
03.12.2023 without any extension being sought, that no Resolution Plan has been 
submitted to this Adjudicating Authority under Section 30(6) of the Code, and 
that the Corporate Debtor has ceased operations and is no longer a going concern. 
The CoC has passed a resol ution in favour of Liquidation with 91.75% majority 
in their 2 nd Meeting of the Committee of Creditors held on 17.11.2023. Under 
these circumstances, this Adjudicating Authority is of the considered view that 
the Corporate Debtor is liable to be liquidated  under Section 33(2) of the Code, 
and accordingly, liquidation proceedings deserve to be initiated in accordance 
with Chapter III of the Code. Accordingly, the Corporate Debtor is ordered to be 
liquidated, and the following consequential order is passed.

ORDER 
 
a. The Corporate Debtor, Shri Vaijanath Industries  Private Limited , is 
directed to be liquidated in accordance with the provisions of Chapter III of 
the Code and applicable regulations. Consequently, the Applicant/RP stands 
relieved subject to procedural/necessary compliances under Section 34(5) 
of the Code. 
 
b. In view of the discussion at Para No.17 of this Order, we deem it appropriate 
to appoint an Insolvency Professional from the panel of Insolvency 
Professionals shared by the IBBI, as Liquida tor in this case. Accordingly, 
we hereby appoint Mr. Neehal Mahamulal Pathan  bearing Registration 
No. IBBI/IPA-001/IP-P-01561/2018-2019/12406, having address at Office 
No. 301, R.S. No.820/A,'Rachana-Anad' Building, E-Ward, Shahupuri, 4th 
Lane, Kolhapur, Shahupuri 4th Lane, Near Amron Battery Showroom, And 
Adv. C. B. Kore Office,  Kolhapur, Maharashtra, 416001 Email id:  
ca[dot]neehal[at]gmail[dot]com having AFA valid upto 31-Dec-26, to act 
as the Liquidator in terms of Section 34 of the Code.  
 
c. The Liquidat or shall initiate the liquidation process as envisaged under 
Chapter III of the Code and the Liquidation Process Regulations applicable 
on the date of passing of this order. He shall take control of all the assets of 
the Corporate Debtor and also continue or institute proceedings in respect 
of any avoidance transactions or fraudulent or wrongful trading, if any, as 
per section 35(1)(l) of the Code. 
 
d. The Liquidator shall be entitled to a fee for conducting the liquidation 
proceedings, as approved by the CoC or in accordance with Regulation 4 of 
the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (Liquidation Process)
